chunk.text: Nine Bits, Three Permission Classes ● Looking at the .bashrc file, -rw-r--r-- starts with - for a regular file, followed by three triplets: rw-, r--, r--. ● The triplets apply to the owner, group and others, in that order. Others means users who match neither owner nor group. ● For a regular file, r allows reading, w allows changing its contents, and x allows execution. A dash means that permission is absent. ● The OS first checks the process’s user identity. If it matches the file owner, only the owner triplet applies. ● Otherwise, a matching group uses the group triplet. If neither matches, the others triplet applies. The triplets are not added together. ● Here, analyst can read and edit .bashrc, while group members and others can read it, provided they can reach its directory. 4

chunk.text: SUBJECT DESCRIPTION 1 Time series analysis comprises the methods used to analyse data indexed in time in order to extract meaningful statistics, identify structure, and produce forecasts. Time series analysis and forecasting are among the most widely applied data science techniques in business, finance, engineering and logistics. Examples of time series include the continuous monitoring of a person's heart rate, hourly readings of air temperature, the daily closing price of a company's stock, monthly rainfall, and yearly sales figures. The field has a well-established theoretical grounding in statistics and dynamic systems theory. This course introduces the most important methods used to model time series data: decomposition, exponential smoothing and ARIMA models.

chunk.text: LEARNING OBJECTIVES The main objective of this course is to provide students with a working methodology and a solid knowledge of the use of time series analysis in business. At the end of the course, students should be able to: Differentiate statistical models for independent observations from models for observations with temporal correlation. Identify patterns in correlated data: trend, seasonality and cycles. Understand and model time series data with exponential smoothing (ETS) and ARIMA models. Understand and apply the most important algorithms in the field. Design an appropriate methodology for each type of time series data (financial, hierarchical, seasonal, intermittent, multiple-seasonal).

chunk.text: 2. ARCHITECTURE 2.1. ADVANTAGES OF CNNs OVER MLPs MLPs use one perceptron for each pixel in an image and the number of weights rapidly becomes • unmanageable for large images. Example: a 224×224 color image has 150,528 inputs, so a single fully connected neuron needs 150,528 weights. A 3×3 convolution filter needs only 27 weights and is reused across the whole image. Another common problem is that MLPs react differently to an input (images) and its shifted version — they • are not translation invariant. Thus, spatial information is lost when the image is flattened (matrix to vector) into an MLP.

result.answer_text: Mintzberg concluded that managers perform ten different roles or sets of behaviors attributable to their jobs [S1]. These roles are divided into three main clusters: Interpersonal, Informational, and Decisional [S2]. The ten roles are: Figurehead, Entrepreneur, Monitor, Disturbance Handler, Leader, Disseminator, Resource Allocator, Liaison, Spokesperson, and Negotiator [S2, S3, S5].
